Weidmann, N.O. (2013). Transformation strategies towards a sustainable Swiss energy system: An energy-economic scenario analysis. Doctoral thesis, ETH Zurich, Diss. ETH No. 21137. https://doi.org/10.3929/ethz-a-009962867

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 17). Swiss MARKAL (SMM-W1/W2) scenario thesis; done in part under the CARMA project. Supplied for the to-get row on the cement price impact of CCS (Habert 2020 ref 139): the thesis does NOT print it. CCS is modelled only for NGCC and centralised gas CHP; CCS in the cement industry is explicitly excluded (p.68: other CCS technologies, including in the cement industry, are not available), there are no cement capture costs, energy penalties or price impacts, and Sutter et al. 2013 is not cited. Extracted: the only technology-level numbers - gas NGCC and NGCHP model inputs for 2010/2030/2050 vintages (Table 3.2, p.28) and the same plants with CCS for 2030/2050 (Table 5.1, p.68): investment, fixed and variable O&M, electrical/thermal efficiency, availability factor and lifetime, based on Hirschberg et al. 2010 (PSI) and own assumptions. CCS rows are whole plants with capture (INCLUDES CAPTURE); capture rate, transport and storage costs are not printed. Costs in CHF2010 (model in USD2000 at 1.35 CHF2010/USD2000). Skipped: PV, wind and large nuclear rows of Table 3.2, car technologies (Appendix A), sector final-energy calibration tables (Ch. 6, e.g. Table 6.8 cement branch final energy by carrier, sector totals) and scenario results.
